title: Distressed schizophrenic patient refusing care
setting: City centre sports event. 38M distressed, schizophrenic, believes men are chasing him, refusing to let responders touch him, breathing heavily.
verdictExplanation: Severe psychiatric crisis with paranoia, distress, rapid breathing, and refusal of necessary care. Sick: call for additional support and protect.

history.history: Believes a group of men are chasing him, ran into the arena for help, refusing medical contact
history.drugs: Antipsychotic medications prescribed (struggling to control symptoms today)

followUp.question: What is your best initial management approach for this paranoid patient?

options.text: Maintain a safe distance, speak in a calm, non-confrontational voice, respect his space, and call for mental health/police support
Physically restrain him immediately to perform a full vital check
Tell him his fears are ridiculous and he must calm down immediately
Leave him alone in the reception and ignore him

followUp.explanation: Psychiatric crisis. Maintain a safe distance, do not crowd or physically touch without consent. Speak in a calm, clear, non-confrontational manner. Call for mental health team or police support if safety is a concern. Never mock or physically restrain a non-violent patient.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Keep safe distance, talk calmly. Coordinate with stewards and call for mental health support.
levelFlags.erNotes: Severe psychiatric crisis. Assess capacity, maintain non-confrontational approach. Check BGL if possible (mimics). Request police/mental health team if patient is a danger to himself or others.
